method: Manual adjudication of each returned answer against the source-verified expectation in questions.json. correctness 0/50/100; completeness = fraction of required answer elements present; faithfulness 100 unless the answer states something the cited/available evidence does not support; hallucination = an unsupported factual assertion (wrong number/name/fact), not merely a wrong refusal.

notes: n=9 per configuration; treat percentages as indicative, not as a stable estimate.
cfgB 'success' (7/9) overstates quality: 0/9 answers are fully correct and 5/9 are non-responsive or irrelevant.
cfgC 'success' (7/9) likewise overstates quality: 0/9 fully correct, 6/9 passed as verified=true while wrong or non-responsive.

Verification did not remove a single wrong answer in either configuration. The 3B verifier converted one workable draft (A01) into an error; the 7B verifier did the same for a different draft and still passed an unsupported year (J01).
Changing the verifier from 3B to 7B changed which answers passed, not how many were correct (0/9 in both) and cost 3.3x the latency.
